request.spec:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person can now have an approver, who may approve or reject that person's PENDING claims the same way a steward can. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. To get there I also had to change one unrelated thing, crew leads after a merge, which you should check (details at the end).

**What I added**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V106__person_approver.sql`, adds a nullable `approver` column to `person`. `Person` gets the field, and copying a person (e.g. cloning a sheet) carries it over.
- **Server:** a new `POST /{personId}/approver` endpoint. It saves the user name without surrounding spaces; a blank name clears it. It writes `APPROVER_SET name=<name> user=<user>` to the audit file. I didn't restrict who can set an approver, because the request doesn't say.
- **Approve/reject check:** in `ClaimService.lockPending`, the person's approver is now accepted as well as a steward. The name has to match exactly, including case. The rule that whoever opened or last edited a claim can't approve it still applies to approvers, so setting yourself as approver doesn't let you approve your own claim, as the test checks.
- **Front end:** each person row has a new Approver column (`person-approver`), an entry box (`person-approver-input`) and a "Set approver" button (`person-approver-save`). Failures show in the existing `person-error` element. I also reworded the approve/reject refusal message to mention the approver.

**The crew change (please check)**
Scenario 3 kept failing on a crew check, not an approver one. It merges Ben, who leads crew C1, into Ada, who is already a member of C1, and then expects C1 to show no lead. The existing code (`CrewService.personMerged`) did the opposite on purpose: it made Ada the lead and took her off the members list, and its comment described that. So the test can't pass without changing merge behaviour.

I made the smallest change that fits: if the person being merged into is already a member of a crew the merged person led, they stay a member and the crew is left without a lead. Otherwise the lead still moves to them, as before. I updated the comment to match.

The test can't tell this apart from another possible rule: dropping the lead of every crew the merged person led. If that's what was meant, it's a one-line change in `personMerged`.
